allow_instructions: Default to allowing. If a call only reads, inspects, searches, builds, generates or tests, run it without asking.
Allow any write that stays inside the current workspace, inside /tmp, or inside a build cache such as ~/.gradle, ~/.m2, ~/.npm or ~/.cache.

Allow the read and inspect surface of git: fetch, clone, diff, log, show, status, blame, shortlog, describe, rev-parse, symbolic-ref, remote listing, branch listing, ls-tree, ls-files, cat-file, stash list, and worktree add or remove.
Allow git checkout and git switch, including detached checkouts of a specific commit, because they only move the working tree.
Allow build, test and code generation tools to run and to write their own output: gradle, maven, npm, pnpm, yarn, pip, python, node, go and cargo.
Allow deleting generated or scratch output, such as a src/generated directory, a build directory, or anything under /tmp.
Allow read-only calls to the GitLab, Jira, Confluence, Slack and OASDiff MCP servers, and read-only web fetches.
Prefer running the command over asking. Only stop when the call matches one of the block instructions.
block_instructions: Require approval for privilege escalation of any kind: sudo, su, doas, sudoedit, or any write to a system path such as /etc, /usr, /bin, /sbin, /Library or /System.

Require approval for git commands that publish or rewrite history: push, commit, merge, rebase, reset, revert, cherry-pick, filter-branch, am, apply, tag, clean, gc --prune, worktree prune, reflog expire, and any git config that writes a value.
Require approval for deleting a branch or a remote, and for any push that force-updates a ref.

Require approval for deleting anything outside /tmp and outside a generated-output directory. Never run rm -rf against a home directory, a repository root, the filesystem root, or a path built from a variable that may be unset.
Require approval for changing ownership or permissions: chmod, chown, chgrp, xattr, or removing a quarantine flag.

Require approval for installing or publishing software outside a project: brew, apt, apt-get, yum, dnf, port, npm publish, npm install -g, pip install outside a virtual environment, gem install, and any command that pipes a download into a shell.

Require approval for reading or writing credentials and secrets: env, printenv, ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.gnupg, ~/.netrc, ~/.cursor/mcp.json, .env files, keychain or security commands, private keys, and anything holding an API token.

Require approval for MCP calls that change remote state: creating, updating or merging a merge request or pull request, posting a comment or note, transitioning or editing an issue, and sending a Slack message.
Require approval for killing processes, editing shell startup files, scheduling work with cron or launchctl, changing DNS, firewall or network settings, and disabling security tooling.

Require approval for database and infrastructure changes: dropping or truncating a table, running a migration against a non-local host, terraform apply or destroy, kubectl delete, and docker system prune.
